_comment: Curated candidate index for the featured races, keyed by AP candidateID. Photos in public/photos/<id>.jpg are public domain or Creative Commons only and were visually verified against a second source on the date in photo.verified. A photo with usage 'needs-permission' is NOT in the repo; photo.remote points at the campaign's own image and must be cleared with the campaign before air. Bios compiled Oct 21 2026 from Wikipedia, Ballotpedia, campaign sites and press; verify before stating on air.

candidates.name: Dan Osborn
candidates.occupation: Industrial mechanic and steamfitter; led the 2021 Kellogg's strike as union local president
candidates.priorOffices: None. 2024 Senate candidate (other seat), lost to Fischer 53.2–46.5
candidates.military: U.S. Navy, 4 years, USS Constellation; later Army National Guard
candidates.notes: Pledges to caucus with neither party. Endorsed by Nebraska Democrats (not a Democrat). Qualified by petition. Averages roughly even to Ricketts +2.

candidates.name: Pete Ricketts
candidates.occupation: U.S. Senator since 2023; former Ameritrade COO
candidates.priorOffices: Governor of Nebraska 2015–2023; appointed to the Senate Jan 2023, won the 2024 special
candidates.notes: 2024 special: 62.6% vs Love (D) 37.4%. Seeking a first full term. Democratic nominee withdrew July 2026.

candidates.name: Chuck Conboy
candidates.occupation: Account manager (unconfirmed)
candidates.notes: Nominated by convention Sept 2026. No FEC receipts. ~2% in one poll.

candidates.name: Robin Richards
candidates.occupation: Business manager, Nebraska Arts Council; party chair
candidates.notes: Democrats alleged a Ricketts-aligned spoiler effort; court kept her on the ballot Sept 2026. $0 FEC receipts.

candidates.name: Mike Marvin
candidates.occupation: Retired public-employee union director
candidates.notes: SUSPENDED campaign Aug 21 2026 (health) and endorsed Osborn; still on the ballot.

candidates.name: Seth Bodnar
candidates.occupation: Former president, University of Montana (2018–Jan 2026); former GE executive
candidates.military: U.S. Army 2003–2022, retired lieutenant colonel; 101st Airborne (Iraq); Green Beret
candidates.education: West Point (first in class, 2001); Oxford (Rhodes Scholar)
candidates.notes: CAUCUS POSITION UNRESOLVED: advisers say neither party; he has not committed on the record. Do not state a pledge on air. Backed by Jon Tester. Quantus (R) Oct 15–18: Alme 44, Bodnar 28, Bankhead 21; his own poll had him +2.

photo.credit: Todd Goodrich / University of Montana via Wikimedia Commons
photo.verified: 2026-10-21 vs Ballotpedia photo: match (2019 photo, no beard then)

candidates.name: Kurt Alme
candidates.occupation: Attorney; former U.S. Attorney for Montana (resigned Mar 2026 to run)
candidates.priorOffices: U.S. Attorney 2017–2020 and 2025–2026; Montana budget director; Dept. of Revenue director. First run for office
candidates.notes: Open seat: Daines withdrew at the filing deadline and endorsed him; Trump endorsed same day. 2020: Daines 55–45. Leads October polls.

photo.license: Public domain (U.S. Dept. of Justice portrait, 2017)
photo.verified: 2026-10-21 vs almeforsenate.com portrait: match. Photo is 9 years old; campaign has a newer one (needs permission)

candidates.name: Alani Bankhead
candidates.occupation: Retired Air Force lieutenant colonel; former counterintelligence special agent; leadership coach
candidates.education: B.A. Penn State; graduate degree, Troy University
candidates.notes: Age approximate (reported 43 in Jan 2026). Refused pressure to withdraw for Bodnar. Polling 12–21%.

photo.license: Public domain (U.S. Air Force video still, 2021)
photo.credit: Tech. Sgt. Nicholas Brown, U.S. Air Force
photo.verified: 2026-10-21 vs alaniformt.com photo: match. LOW QUALITY (540px video frame); request campaign headshot for air

candidates.name: Kyle Austin
candidates.occupation: Pharmacist; pharmacy owner; farmer
candidates.notes: Disavowed by the state Libertarian Party. Polling 2–6%.

candidates.name: Todd Achilles
candidates.occupation: Former tech executive (T-Mobile, HTC, HP; CEO of Evoca); public policy lecturer, Boise State
candidates.priorOffices: Idaho House, District 16B, as a Democrat (2024–July 2025); left the party to run
candidates.military: U.S. Army armor officer 1992–1995; tank commander, two Persian Gulf deployments
candidates.education: B.A. Claremont McKenna; MBA and M.A. Washington; M.P.P. Berkeley
candidates.notes: Pledged Oct 7 2026 to caucus with neither party and to serve no more than two terms. Democratic nominee withdrew in his favor. Polls split: Risch campaign poll Risch 49–24; ATR Sept: Achilles 46–39.

photo.verified: 2026-10-21 vs achillesforidaho.com photo: match. LOW QUALITY video still; request campaign photo for air

candidates.name: Jim Risch
candidates.occupation: U.S. Senator since 2009; chair, Foreign Relations Committee
candidates.priorOffices: Ada County prosecutor; Idaho Senate (26 years); Lt. Governor; Governor 2006–07
candidates.education: B.S. forestry and J.D., University of Idaho
candidates.notes: Age 83, seeking a 4th term. 2020: 62.6% vs Jordan (D) 33.2%. Rated Safe R.

photo.verified: 2026-10-21 vs 2021 committee photo and senatorrisch.com: match. Portrait is 17 years old; request a current official portrait from the Senate office (also public domain)

candidates.name: Natalie Fleming
candidates.occupation: Software developer
candidates.notes: Perennial candidate. Polling 3–9%. Age approximate.

candidates.name: Matt Loesby
candidates.occupation: Software engineer; Libertarian Party of Idaho officer
candidates.notes: Polling 2–5%. $0 raised.

candidates.name: Brian Bengs
candidates.occupation: Retired Air Force JAG officer and attorney; former National Park Service ranger; former professor
candidates.priorOffices: None. 2022 Democratic Senate nominee (lost to Thune 69.6–26.2)
candidates.military: U.S. Navy enlisted at 17; U.S. Air Force JAG about 19 years, retired 2016 as lieutenant colonel
candidates.notes: Age approximate. Pledged (Oct 12 2026, with Osborn and Bodnar) to caucus with neither party. Forward Party endorsement. Rounds-sponsored poll Oct 2026: Rounds 54, Bengs 37. Two-way race after the Democrat withdrew.

photo.verified: 2026-10-21 campaign candid vs Ballotpedia photo: match. The only public-domain image (pre-2004 Air Force portrait) could not be visually matched to him today and is not used

candidates.name: Mike Rounds
candidates.occupation: U.S. Senator since 2015; former insurance and real estate business owner
candidates.notes: 2020: 65.7% vs Ahlers (D). Trump-endorsed. Rated Safe R.

candidates.name: Kevin Kiley
candidates.residence: Rocklin (verify it lies inside the new district before saying so)
candidates.occupation: U.S. Representative (CA-3) since 2023; attorney; former teacher
candidates.notes: Left the Republican Party Mar 9 2026 after Prop 50 redrew his district; the House's only independent. Says he will join neither caucus if re-elected. New CA-6 is D+5. Polls: Pan 39–35 (July); 37–37 (pro-Kiley, Sept). Forecasters favor Pan.

candidates.name: Richard Pan
candidates.occupation: Pediatrician; UC Davis professor; former state senator
candidates.education: B.S. Johns Hopkins; M.D. Pittsburgh; M.P.H. Harvard
candidates.notes: Author of California's 2015 school-vaccine law. Second in the top-two primary. Favored by forecasters.

photo.license: Public domain (California State Senate photo, per Commons)

candidates.name: Bill Hill
candidates.occupation: Commercial fisherman; retired educator; co-owner, Bristol Bay Brailer
candidates.priorOffices: None elected. Superintendent, Bristol Bay Borough schools 2013–2023; Alaska Superintendent of the Year
candidates.notes: Dena'ina Athabascan. Age approximate (AP: 57). Endorsed by Alaska Democrats after their leading candidate withdrew. Has declined to say which party he would caucus with. Ranked choice: needs transfers. PPP Oct 14–15: Begich 45, Hill 44.

photo.license: CC0 (public domain dedication by the campaign)
photo.credit: Bill Hill for Alaskans via Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Nick Begich III
candidates.occupation: U.S. Representative since 2025; software entrepreneur
candidates.priorOffices: None before Congress; lost to Peltola twice in 2022
candidates.notes: 2024: beat Peltola 51.2–48.8 after three RCV rounds. Rated Likely R.

candidates.name: Eric Hafner
candidates.residence: Federal prison, Otisville, N.Y. (has never lived in Alaska)
candidates.occupation: Federal prisoner; perennial candidate
candidates.notes: Serving 20 years for threats against officials. Not endorsed by Alaska Democrats. Polling 5–9%.

candidates.name: James McDermott
candidates.occupation: Writer; tutor
candidates.notes: Finished 8th in the primary; advanced after withdrawals. Age approximate. Polling 1–5%.

candidates.name: Sarah Zabel
candidates.occupation: Retired Air Force major general; author
candidates.military: U.S. Air Force 1987–2018, retired major general; cyber and communications; Bronze Star (Qatar 2003–04); vice director, DISA
candidates.education: B.S. computer science, Air Force Academy; master's degrees incl. Army War College
candidates.notes: Says she would caucus with neither party. Forward Party endorsement. Polling ~5–6% in three-way surveys (July); her own poll had a two-way race at Zabel 42, Fulcher 39.

photo.license: Public domain (official U.S. Air Force portrait)
photo.verified: 2026-10-21 vs 2018 DVIDS photo and campaign headshot: match. Uniformed portrait; the campaign's civilian headshot needs permission

candidates.name: Russ Fulcher
candidates.occupation: U.S. Representative since 2019; former Micron executive
candidates.priorOffices: Idaho Senate 2005–2014; lost 2014 GOP governor primary
candidates.notes: 2024: 71.0% vs Peterson 25.4%. Seeking a 5th term. Rated Safe R.

photo.credit: U.S. House Office of Photography / Franmarie Metzler

candidates.name: Kaylee Peterson
candidates.occupation: Grassroots organizer and political strategist; former president, Idaho Young Democrats
candidates.priorOffices: None; Democratic nominee for ID-1 in 2022 (26.3%) and 2024 (25.4%)
candidates.notes: Third run against Fulcher. Age approximate. Polling 27–35% (July).

photo.verified: 2026-10-21 campaign photo vs Ballotpedia headshot: match. No free-licensed image exists

candidates.name: Brendan Gomez
candidates.notes: Remains on the ballot after a Sept 2026 guilty plea (sexual exploitation material); sentencing Nov 16. Age approximate. $0 raised.
